markdown:
*1d4 slashing, 3 lb., finesse, reach*

A whip is a tool or weapon designed to strike humans or other animals to exert control through pain compliance or fear of pain. They can also be used without inflicting pain, for audiovisual cues, such as in equestrianism. A hunting whip combines a firm stick (the stock or handle) with a flexible line (the lash or thong).

Whips such as the "cat o' nine tails" and knout are specifically developed for flagellation as a means of inflicting corporal punishment or torture on human targets. Certain religious practices and BDSM activities involve the self-use of whips or the use of whips between consenting partners. Misuse on non-humans may be considered animal cruelty, and misuse on humans may be viewed as assault.

Or hot. To each their own.

### Features

- ***On Your Knees.*** When attacking someone who is prone and more than 5 feet away from you with this weapon, you ignore the disadvantage caused by them being prone.
- ***In My Grasp.*** When using a whip, you may attempt to grapple an opponent with it using the standard rules for grappling, even though you are not adjacent to the creature. All the same limitations for grappling apply, but the person initiating the grapple with a whip is able to move around the full distance of their reach around their grappled opponent. Moving in this way does not provoke attacks of opportunity from the grappled target to the grappler. While maintaining a grapple in this way, you may not use the whip to attack anyone else but the grappled target until the grapple is broken. Someone using a whip to grapple an opponent cannot use special grapple actions unless they are adjacent to the creature they're grappling.
